summary: Gap-repair selection (gapped_rules_needing_repair, capped at kMaxGapRepairsPerKick=32) walked an unordered_map in bucket order with no rotation; with >32 simultaneously-gapped rules the same subset was returned every kick, starving the rest indefinitely even after connectivity recovered.

classification_rationale: A design/implementation defect in code this branch introduced, not a wording issue.
adjudication_rationale: Confirmed real defect (not an acceptable D1d-class trade-off); root cause sharper than reported (cap counted listed entries including in-flight repairs, not eligible ones); specified least-recently-attempted round-robin, eligibility-filtered at the source, as the fix mechanism.

summary: The gap ledger and loss counters (GuardianLegacySinkExecutor::State) were pure in-process fields; an agent restart mid-outage discarded them, so the fleet gauge (yuzu_fleet_guardian_legacy_sink_gap_rules) read as "resolved" identically to a genuine repair, with no way for an operator to distinguish the two.
trigger: agent process restart while a gap is open
classification_rationale: Design/implementation defect, not wording.
adjudication_rationale: Split into a signal half (fixable in-process, no durable spool needed) and a history half (genuinely requires the durable spool D1d declined — filed as #4888 instead of attempted here). Specified a small restart-durable KV marker (counters + gap snapshots, no event payloads) via the agent's existing KvStore, matching the pre-existing guardian_persist_baseline/read_baseline_record pattern.

summary: An interior compliance transition (e.g. drift.detected) refused at capacity while bracketing events for the same rule are admitted self-clears via the seq-guard with no repair ever synthesized; the server's audit history shows continuous compliance through a real violation window even though current state is accurate. events_lost still increments (aggregate signal survives) but per-rule attribution and the compensating census correction are lost.
trigger: capacity exhaustion during a stall, with a real bracketing event admitted before the next heartbeat kick
classification_rationale: Behavioural gap in shipped code, not wording; de-escalated rather than fully closed per adjudication below.
adjudication_rationale: Confirmed as the accepted D1/D1d design trade-off (the gap ledger is a census-integrity mechanism, never an audit-history log) rather than a new defect. Fully closing it requires a durable spool of lost-event content, explicitly out of scope for #4783 — filed as issue #4888. De-escalated (not silenced) via two changes that alter the epistemic facts: a per-loss attribution log (rule_id + loss kind, at the moment of loss) and events_lost becoming restart-durable via the UP-3 mechanism, so "something was lost, on this rule" survives a process restart even when the ledger itself self-clears.

summary: legacy_sink_kick() (heartbeat thread, off mtx_) and stop()'s final persist (shutdown thread, under mtx_) both ran an unsynchronized snapshot->decide->write->record-gen sequence coordinated only by a standalone atomic; a late in-flight kick() could resume after a concurrent stop() had already persisted fresher data and overwrite it with its own stale snapshot, silently regressing the restart-durable ledger UP-3's fix exists to protect. A pure CAS on the atomic alone would not have closed this (the physical KV write order between the two threads was the actual hazard, not just the tracked generation value). TSan cannot detect this class (no unsynchronized memory access, a logical check-then-act ordering bug).
trigger: an in-flight legacy_sink_kick() persist racing GuardianEngine::stop()'s unconditional final persist, reachable via agent.cpp's documented shutdown ordering (stop() called before quiesce_run_workers() joins the heartbeat thread)
classification_rationale: A genuine new concurrency defect introduced by the UP-3/UP-4 fix itself, not wording.

summary: UP-2's fairness proof (every eligible gap repaired within ceil(n/32) kicks) assumes a stable-or-growing gapped-rule population; a rule that fully clears and reopens faster than the heartbeat interval gets a fresh last_attempt_kick=0 each time, re-entering at the front of the rotation. Under sustained load with several such flapping rules, a persistently-failing rule (nonzero last_attempt_kick) could be pushed back indefinitely. Impact muted: current guard state stays accurate regardless; only the synthesized repair REPORT is delayed.
classification_rationale: A gap in the UP-2 fairness guarantee's own stated proof, found during Gate 8 re-review of that fix.
waiver_rationale: Accepted, documented limitation - not fixed given the muted impact (current state stays accurate; only report timing is affected).

summary: legacy_sink_kick() performs a synchronous snapshot+serialize+blocking KV write on the heartbeat thread when change_gen has advanced. Payload is naturally bounded by open-gap count; a pathologically slow disk plus a very large rule count could measurably stretch one heartbeat tick. Same synchronous-KV-on-heartbeat pattern journal_maintenance_tick() already uses.
classification_rationale: A real, bounded latency risk in new code, consistent with an already-accepted pre-existing pattern.
waiver_rationale: Accepted - matches the existing journal_maintenance_tick() precedent, no new architectural risk.
